about: The edit bus every runtime keeps per open window (DESIGN 5.29): a record of the person's edits, each a message with the part, its scope (its form or panel, or itself), what it changed (each name of the window's data, or `#parts.<name>` for a part's own text or tick, with its value before and after) and the database steps its handler made. A case starts with the window's data as `start` and runs `steps` in order. `edit`: the person ended an edit of `part` in `scope`, and the window's data is now `data` (with what the edit's handler changed); `steps` are the database steps that handler made. `drag`: a part's edit goes on (a canvas's drag before its drop): the window's data is now `data`, with the handler's `steps`, and the edit is not ended. `reply`: a handler that is no edit replied with `data`; the edits start from there. `undo` and `redo` take back or do again the last edit of that scope: `data` is the window's data after it, `steps` the database steps taken back (last first) or done again (first first), `refused` when the database refused it (the edit stays where it was), and `nothing` when the scope has no edit to take back or do again. An edit that changed nothing and made no step is no message; a new edit ends what could be done again in its scope, and only there.

cases.name: a form walks back field by field, the last first, and does them again
what a handler that is no edit changed is not taken back
an edit and what its handler saved are one, taken back together
a drag and its drop are one edit, its steps taken back last first
an edit that changed nothing and made no step is no message
a new edit ends what could be done again in its scope, and only there
a refused undo keeps the edit, to be tried again
a part's own text is part of its edit
an undo puts back only what the edit changed, keeping what changed since elsewhere
